description: We are a passionate team of tech enthusiasts interested in AI/ML, software development, data science, and space exploration. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we aim to build an AI-powered platform that transforms NASA's microgravity combustion research into meaningful fire-safety insights. We value collaboration, innovation, and practical problem-solving. We welcome motivated members with skills in AI/ML, Python, data analysis, frontend development, scientific research, and UI/UX design.
summary:
PyroNull: NASA Combustion Intelligence

PyroNull is a web dashboard, backed by a FastAPI service, that turns NASA’s Physical Science Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data into fire-safety insights for human space exploration.

Users can search and explore investigations such as BASS, SAME, FLEX and ACME. They can compare experiments side by side on fuels, oxygen concentration, pressure and airflow, and ask a research assistant evidence-linked questions. A Mission Intelligence module ranks investigations by relevance to habitat scenarios such as the Moon base, a Mars surface base, a pressurized rover or a spacecraft. It also flags research gaps and generates reports. A Predictive Lab runs machine-learning models trained on PSI data, including burn time, ignition outcome and flame temperature. Each prediction ships with its error metrics and an explicit warning about the domain it was trained on.

This answers the challenge’s call to find, compare and interpret overwhelming data, to support predictive modeling of flammability, and to highlight research that informs prevention, detection and suppression.

It matters because crews returning to the Moon and going on to Mars will breathe oxygen-enriched, reduced-pressure air, which makes materials far more flammable. Helping engineers and researchers quickly find the right evidence makes those missions safer.
details:
What it does

PyroNull (FIREWISE AI) is a web dashboard that helps researchers and engineers find, compare and interpret NASA microgravity combustion investigations for spacecraft fire safety. It has six areas:

  • Investigation Explorer: search and filter investigations by fuel, domain (prevention, detection, suppression) and keywords.
  • Compare Experiments: side-by-side comparison of conditions such as oxygen level, pressure and flow.
  • Mission Intelligence: pick a mission profile (spacecraft, station, Moon base, Mars base, pressurized rover) and get an explainable relevance ranking, the evidence behind each result, its limitations, and gaps in coverage. It can also assemble these into a report.
  • Fire Risk Intelligence and Scientific AI Assistant: evidence-linked interpretation and Q&A.
  • Predictive Lab: machine-learning models trained on PSI data. They estimate burn time (PSI-159), ignition class (PSI-159), flame temperature, mixture fraction and pressure rise (PSI-10), fuel class (PSI-107) and FLEX flame outcome (PSI-69).

Benefits and intended impact

It turns an overwhelming pile of experiments into clear, comparable answers. The aim is to shorten the path from “what has NASA tested?” to “what applies to my habitat?”, especially for the oxygen-enriched, reduced-pressure atmospheres planned for the Moon and Mars.

Tools

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4, TanStack Query, Recharts, react-hook-form.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn.
  • Machine learning: scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, joblib, with PyTorch and TensorFlow for some models.
  • Hosting: Render.

Creativity

Honesty about uncertainty is built into the design. Every prediction returns its error metrics (MAE, RMSE, R²), its limitations and an explicit out-of-domain warning, for example “not a fire-risk probability”. Mission scenarios keep unspecified conditions as unknown instead of guessing. Rankings are explainable heuristics, not a black box.

Factors considered

  • Safety: we made no claim of certified fire-risk prediction, since PSI has no partial-gravity data yet.
  • Data provenance: we kept it transparent, with demo records marked.
  • Audience: professors, students and aerospace engineers.
  • Reliability: the frontend retries while the free-tier backend wakes from sleep.
